description: Who We Are You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today. We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover. Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI. Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate. Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale. About the team Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, ecommerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people. About the role We’re looking for a senior data engineer to build and operate LCM’s training-data platform, covering acquisition, processing, synthetic generation, quality evaluation and dataset versioning. Our core data includes events, sessions, orders, catalogues and feedback, supplemented by external sources and generated examples. In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work with scientists and ML engineers to turn these sources into reproducible datasets and measure how changes to the data affect model performance. You’ll also build tools and agents that automate preparation, task design and quality analysis. In the first three months, we expect you to take ownership of a part of the platform, such as a pipeline, the dataset versioning layer or the quality checks, deliver a reproducible dataset that a research project uses in a training run, and work with scientists to measure how your data changes affect model quality. What the role involves Build acquisition and processing pipelines for portfolio data and relevant public and licensed sources, including connectors and content extraction. Turn commerce records into ordered histories and link behaviour to outcomes without leaking future information. Develop the shared platform for inspecting sources, configuring processing and publishing training datasets. Operate distributed workflows, monitor reliability and cost, and implement access controls and retention requirements. Work with scientists, engineers and the relevant teams on data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories. Implement dataset versioning and lineage across source snapshots, processing code and dataset configurations, so releases can be reproduced and traced to the training runs that used them. Build quality checks for completeness, freshness, duplication, extraction accuracy and coverage. Combine automated checks with sampled review to investigate problems that aggregate metrics can miss. Provide tools for source tagging, sampling and weighting, and maintain evaluation datasets with temporal splits and overlap checks. Work with scientists on controlled comparisons to establish whether data changes improve model quality. Build synthetic data pipelines supporting pre- and post-training, including instruction examples, preference data and agent trajectories. Implement generation, validation, scoring and filtering. Work with the research team to measure how the generated data affects model performance, and manage generation throughput and cost. Build agents that turn catalogue sources into training datasets: propose tasks based on available data and target model capabilities, configure processing and generation, curate outputs and investigate quality failures. Keep agent actions traceable and validate proposed changes before dataset release. Minimum qualifications At least five years of relevant data engineering experience, including ownership of substantial production pipelines. Strong Python and SQL, with experience writing tested, maintainable code. Hands-on experience with distributed processing using Spark, Ray, Beam or a comparable framework. Experience with cloud storage, workflow orchestration and operating pipelines through source changes, failures and backfills. Practical knowledge of data quality, versioning and lineage, and the ability to translate evolving research requirements into reliable implementations. Preferred qualifications Experience with LLM datasets, commerce data, content extraction, synthetic data generation or agents for data tasks. Experience with AWS, Databricks or EMR. Strong distributed-data engineering experience is welcome without prior experience on an LLM team. What we offer Ownership of the platform supplying LCM’s training and evaluation data, with direct collaboration with researchers and ML engineers. Access to proprietary commerce datasets, distributed processing infrastructure and models for generation and evaluation. Scope to make technical decisions and build reusable tools across portfolio companies. Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems. Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants. A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role. Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro. If you’ve built data systems at scale and want to help shape what a foundation model can do, we’d like to hear from you. Tell us about something you’ve built, the challenges involved and the difference it made. Why Prosus? At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next. Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing. Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page . Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have. Want to know more about life at Prosus? Explore our culture and values . Find more English Speaking Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. Role Summary We are seeking an Applied AI, Forward Deployed Engineer to build customer use cases on top of the Mistral stack for our defense, government and critical-infrastructure customers. You will turn "we have agents" into "we shipped something a client uses." This role is about composing cybersecurity-related agentic workflows focused on cyberdefense, configuring harnesses for real-world scenarios, and delivering value directly to clients — often in sovereign, on-premises or classified environments. You will work with some of the most security-sensitive organizations in the world: government agencies, sovereign institutions and operators of critical infrastructure. They need AI that is powerful, controllable and deployable on their terms. Why this role: you will build some of the first AI-for-cyberdefense systems deployed in real government and defense environments, on frontier models you can influence. You will work in a tight-knit team alongside elite experts in DFIR and cyberdefense — people who are passionate about their craft — and the patterns you implement at customer sites feed directly back into Mistral's internal use cases and products. Few roles put this much frontier technology this close to missions that matter. What You Will Do Client-Facing Agentic Solutions You'll individually help deploy into production use cases with considerable business impact, with defense and government cybersecurity assignments as a priority You'll work on state-of-the-art GenAI applications, driving a crucial technological transformation together with our customers Tackle iconic customer use cases that no existing solution on the market can address — from custom configuration of cybersecurity harnesses for cloud defense, to agentic alert triage and investigation, incident response automation, detection engineering, threat intelligence analysis, and security log analysis at scale You'll be involved in pre-sales calls to understand potential customers' needs, challenges, and aspirations, providing technical guidance on our products and explaining Mistral technologies to various stakeholders You'll collaborate with our product and science teams to continuously improve our product and model capabilities based on customer feedback Ship secure by design. Apply least-privilege access, secrets management, authN/authZ best practices, audit logging, human-in-the-loop approval for high-impact actions, and defenses against prompt injection and data exfiltration in agentic systems Design and run evaluations that measure technical correctness, operational value and safety, so customers can trust what is being deployed Own deployment end to end — observability, reliability, cost and latency tuning — including on-premises and air-gapped setups where customers require them Our Principles We care about people and outputs What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before No politics. Low ego, high standards We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it Security & Compliance criteria Eligibility: must hold citizenship in the target territory (France for now). Clearable: must meet all local requirements for high-level security clearance About You You are fluent in French, with strong English — this customer set works in French You have 5+ years building systems in a cybersecurity context — SOC automation, DFIR automation, detection engineering, security tooling, or similar — with a record of operating what you ship in production On top of that, you have 1+ year of hands-on experience building agentic or LLM-based systems, ideally in production — with a deep understanding of the concepts: prompting and context engineering, RAG, tool use, agentic orchestration, evaluations, guardrails, and knowing when to use each. If you don't have the production year yet, deep familiarity and the drive to learn fast in real, constrained environments is what we're looking for You have strong technical coding skills in Python, plus full-stack experience: APIs, back-end services and front-end interfaces (e.g. TypeScript/React) You have strong communication skills, with an ability to explain complex technical concepts in simple terms to both technical and non-technical audiences Ideally, you have: Experience with security tooling or workflows (SIEM, SOAR, EDR/XDR, threat intel) Experience as a Security Operations Engineer, Detection & Response Engineer, or Incident Response Engineer Experience as a Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Architect, Solutions Engineer Prior work with government, defense, or national-security customers A bias toward action and delivery — you ship fast, operate independently with a customer-led mindset, and reuse internal building blocks effectively Strong problem-solving abilities, attention to detail, and a collaborative attitude What We Offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page . Privacy Policy Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy . Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate. Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale. About the team Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people. About the role We’re looking for experienced applied scientists in two tracks: pre-training, and post-training and continual learning. Each scientist will own a focused research direction within a track. The areas below describe the team’s research agenda; we are looking for depth in one or more of them. The role involves designing experiments, writing the code to run them, analysing results and developing training methods that other teams can use. Scientists own the research questions, training objectives and evidence needed to decide whether a change works, and work with ML engineers to turn successful experiments into reliable training runs. We are a team of around 30 engineers with a flat structure, working directly with portfolio companies to define problems, evaluate models and bring successful work into production. In the first three months, the expectation is to establish strong baselines in a chosen research area, develop and evaluate an improvement, and work with the relevant teams to test it in a downstream application. Track 1: Pre-training This track focuses on continued pre-training of open-weight models on commerce data, including how we represent that data, allocate training compute and transfer capabilities to smaller models. Research areas include: Studying scaling behaviour, data mixtures and compute allocation to decide what goes into the next training run. Developing mid-training methods, including data refinement, annealing schedules, context extension and alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants. Designing training sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, and studying how representations transfer across companies, languages and commerce categories. Building synthetic data pipelines and measuring their contribution through controlled comparisons with real data. Distilling the base model into smaller models, including through on-policy distillation, and measuring the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency. Developing evaluations that help select pre-training runs and predict downstream performance, including checks for temporal leakage, generalisation to new users and items, and retention of existing capabilities. Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation: pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data, using synthetic and real tables and comparing results with established tabular methods. Relevant experience includes continued pre-training or mid-training, data mixture research, scaling laws, tokenisation, entity representations, distillation, or tabular foundation models such as TabPFN and TabICL. Track 2: Post-training and continual learning This track focuses on adapting LCM to commerce tasks and learning from interactions after deployment. The goal is to turn signals from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio into regular updates to model weights, while retaining the capabilities the model has already learned. Research areas include: Developing post-training methods using supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation such as DPO, and reinforcement learning with verifiable or learned rewards, including GRPO and PPO. Learning from session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback. This includes data selection, credit assignment and reward design that account for exposure bias, delayed outcomes and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value. Studying how to combine new interactions with historical data, how frequently to update models, when an update is ready for deployment, and how to preserve performance as user behaviour and catalogues change. Building RL environments with simulated users, catalogues and multi-step commerce tasks, including inspecting trajectories, validating rewards and testing whether improvements in simulation transfer to real interactions. Developing reward models and LLM-based graders, calibrating them against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and testing for reward hacking, sycophancy and excessive concentration on popular items. Training decision models for rankings, offers and promotions using contextual bandits or offline RL, with off-policy evaluation to estimate value and uncertainty, identify gaps in the available evidence and inform controlled online experiments. Developing automated experiments that propose and test changes to training methods, prompts, tools or agent control flow, evaluated on held-out tasks and regression tests before acceptance. Relevant experience includes language-model post-training, reinforcement learning, reward modelling, agent training environments, continual learning, or offline RL and bandits applied to real decisions. The training experience required will depend on the research direction. Responsibilities across both tracks Define success with portfolio teams and evaluate models against strong baselines, including existing production systems, accounting for inference cost, latency and the business outcome the model is meant to improve. Design reproducible experiments with appropriate ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis, using future-period and held-out evaluations, and test whether offline improvements hold online. Work with data and engineering teams on provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories. Publish research and contribute models, benchmarks, environments and training methods to open source where the work and data can be shared. Mentor colleagues, review experiment designs and communicate findings clearly enough to support training and deployment decisions. Minimum qualifications A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field. At least five years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with hands-on experience designing and running model-training experiments. For Track 1, this should include pre-training or mid-training of language models. For Track 2, it should include language-model post-training, or reinforcement learning and decision-model training relevant to the specialisation. Evidence of original research through papers, released models, public benchmarks, open-source projects or significant research contributions to deployed systems. Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with experience implementing experiments and debugging training runs in a shared research codebase. Work on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training. Sound experimental judgment, including strong baselines, statistical analysis and the willingness to report negative results. Clear written and verbal communication. Preferred qualifications Experience implementing and debugging training methods in frameworks such as Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, NeMo RL, verl or OpenRLHF, depending on the chosen track. Research in recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs or user behaviour modelling. Experience with synthetic data, model distillation or compression for production. Experience working with marketplace or commerce data and evaluating changes through online experiments. What we offer Autonomy to design experiments and make technical decisions within your research direction. Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking. The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people. Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems. An uncapped budget to recruit and mentor research interns for your projects, with access to candidates through our connections with leading universities. Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants. A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role. Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro. How to apply If you want to work on these problems, we would like to hear from you. We build from the evals: we define how success will be measured before developing a capability, and use the results to guide training, model selection and deployment. We already have hundreds of evaluations spanning domain knowledge, commerce and gaming, with plans to expand their coverage, depth and scale. This work builds on ProLLM, the public benchmarking platform we ran for real-world use cases until our coding assistant benchmarks became saturated. Since then it has been a private benchmarking platform for Prosus companies. We plan to open it again to publish our commerce benchmarks, covering both agentic and decision-making tasks. We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own the development of these evaluations and the platform that runs them. The work involves defining meaningful tasks, curating evaluation data, implementing reliable scoring, investigating model behaviour and making results useful for research and product decisions. In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work directly with applied scientists, training engineers and domain experts. You’ll help teams contribute evaluations and build the infrastructure and automation needed to run them throughout model development. In the first three months, we expect you to take technical ownership of part of the evaluation platform, deliver a set of new or improved evaluations with curated data and calibrated difficulty, and work with scientists to use them in a training or release decision. What the role involves Design evaluations with scientists and domain experts, translating intended capabilities into representative tasks, datasets and success criteria. Cover current applications and capabilities we want future models to acquire. Curate evaluation data and calibrate task difficulty, so that evaluations are neither saturated nor out of reach and still separate models of different quality. Work with domain experts on sourcing, annotation and review, within data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy requirements. Own the development and operation of the evaluation platform across training checkpoints, deployed models and external baselines. Support distributed execution, reproducible configurations, trace inspection and comparison of results, while managing runtime and cost. Develop programmatic checks, outcome-based scoring and LLM-based graders. Calibrate automated judgments against expert reviews, investigate disagreements and test whether graders reward superficial answers or reject valid solutions. Analyse model outputs and agent trajectories, including tool calls, environment state and task outcomes. Distinguish model failures from problems in the evaluation, quantify uncertainty and explain what changed between versions. Maintain versioned tasks, datasets, graders and environments, with protected held-out tests and contamination checks. Expand coverage as models improve, retaining useful regression tests and adding harder tasks where existing tests no longer distinguish performance. Prepare commerce benchmarks for public release on ProLLM, including public mirror sets and evaluation code, where the data can be shared. Integrate evaluations into training and release workflows, with dashboards and regression checks that support concrete decisions. Work with portfolio teams to establish whether offline improvements correspond to better outcomes in online experiments. Build tools and agents that help generate candidate tasks, run evaluations and investigate failures, validating their outputs before adoption. Review contributions and mentor engineers so teams can extend the suite consistently. Minimum qualifications At least five years of ML or software engineering experience, including substantial hands-on work building and evaluating ML systems. Experience owning evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or model-quality systems that informed training or deployment decisions. Strong Python and experience with PyTorch, Transformers or comparable ML libraries, alongside reliable production software development.
